title: He lowers the proud, so no bully gets the last word
subtitle: Al-Khafid: the One who brings down arrogance and oppression with perfect justice
intro: Al-Khafid (الخافض) means the Abaser, the One who lowers: He brings down the arrogant, the oppressor and falsehood, in this life or the next, always with perfect justice. For anyone who has been looked down on it is a comfort, not a threat, and for the ego in each of us it is a gentle warning.

root.sense: Khafd is to lower or bring down: lowering the voice, lowering a wing, low-lying land. In Arabic grammar it names the case that brings a word's ending down. The picture is of something that stood high being set low, whether it falls by force or bends down gently by choice.

row.title: Power always gets away with it
Every false height falls
sub: He lowers it in His time

knowing: Al-Khafid is the One who lowers. He brings down those who raise themselves against Him and against His creation: the arrogant, the tyrant, the person who builds a name on other people's backs. The Prophet ﷺ described Allah as the One who lowers the scale and raises it (Sahih Muslim): every rise and fall in the world is in His hand. This name is narrated in the well-known list of names in Jami' al-Tirmidhi, and scholars stress that it should be said together with Ar-Rafi', the One who raises.

{idea}His lowering is never random and never unjust.{/idea} He does not bring anyone down for being poor, plain or unknown. He brings down what deserves to fall: pride, oppression, the lie dressed up as truth. Even this is mercy. Unchecked tyranny would crush the weak, so His lowering protects the world. And sometimes it is mercy for the one who falls, when losing status breaks an arrogance that would otherwise have ruined their Hereafter.

People lower one another out of envy and rivalry. Allah has no rival and envies no one; He lowers as a just judge gives a verdict, with full knowledge. He created the human being in the finest form, then returns him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do good (95:4-6). The lowness He describes there is the place a person drifts to when they turn away from Him.
seeing: Surat al-Waqi'ah opens by describing the Day of Resurrection as the event that brings some down and raises others up (56:1-3). Kings who were obeyed without question will stand with nothing. People nobody noticed will be lifted. History already gives small previews: Pharaoh called himself the highest lord and ended under the waves.

Think of the oppressors who stood over the bodies of prophets and believers, sure that they had won. Their power had an expiry date they could not see. The Prophet ﷺ also said that Allah raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it (Sahih Muslim). The same Quran lifts the one who lives by it and lowers the one who turns his back on it. The ranking that counts is not the world's ranking.
trusting: If someone has humiliated you, whether a manager, a relative or a whole system, you do not have to carry the job of revenge. Al-Khafid sees everything. {reward}You can leave the bringing down to Him and keep your own hands clean.{/reward} His timing may not match yours. He is not unaware of what the wrongdoers do; He only gives them time (14:42).

Then turn the name inward, gently. Where am I raising myself? A sharp comment, quiet contempt for someone less educated, a need to be seen as better. {trap}The ego that climbs on other people is the first thing Al-Khafid brings down.{/trap} The safest place is low before Him in prostration. The Prophet ﷺ said that no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him (Sahih Muslim).
loving: A world without Al-Khafid would belong to the loudest and the cruellest. Because He lowers, the weak have a defender, the slandered will be cleared, and no tyrant has the final word. {idea}You love Him the way you love a just protector who stands between you and those who would trample you.{/idea} And because He raises those who lower themselves to Him, the way up is open to everyone.
now: A colleague presents your work as their own in the meeting and everyone nods along. Your face burns on the walk back to your desk. Al-Khafid saw the whole thing, and no stolen height lasts with Him. Write down the facts calmly, speak up fairly if you can, and let go of needing to see them fall today.
old: When arrogant people win, I feel the world simply rewards whoever pushes hardest.
new: Every false height is temporary, because Allah lowers pride and oppression with perfect justice in His own time.
try: Do one thing today that lowers your ego on purpose: admit a mistake out loud, or thank someone you usually overlook.

dua.text: Ya Khafid, Ya Rafi', lower the pride in my heart before it lowers me, protect me from the arrogance of others, and raise me through humility before You.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name together with Ar-Rafi', especially when you are wronged by the powerful or notice pride rising in yourself.

pairs.why: He lowers and He raises: the two names describe one balance of justice and are said together.
His lowering is never arbitrary; Al-Adl means every fall He decrees is fully deserved and fairly weighed.

faq.a: Al-Khafid means the Abaser or the One who lowers. Allah brings down the arrogant, oppressors and falsehood, in this world or the next, with perfect justice and wisdom. The name is narrated in the well-known list of names in Jami' al-Tirmidhi and is mentioned together with Ar-Rafi', the Exalter.

faq.q: Should a believer be afraid of the name Al-Khafid?
faq.a: Not in a way that crushes hope. Allah lowers pride, injustice and rebellion, not the poor, the weak or the sincere. For the oppressed the name is a promise that no tyrant wins in the end. For everyone it is a gentle reminder that humility before Allah is the way to be raised.

faq.q: Where does the meaning of Al-Khafid appear in the Quran and hadith?
faq.a: Surat al-Waqi'ah describes the Day of Resurrection as one that brings some down and raises others (56:3). In Sahih Muslim the Prophet ﷺ described Allah as lowering the scale and raising it, and said Allah raises some people by the Quran and lowers others by it.
